comments.body: Design question from the owner, 2026-11-06: perhaps a banner should be much smaller than eight source lines. It is a notice that a message arrived and a place to answer it, not where a message of several paragraphs is meant to be read; the conversation is. A much tighter cap (a line or two, or a fixed drawn height) would settle the overflow by design and keep the stack out of the middle of the panes, at the cost of more trips to the conversation for a question that needs its context to answer.
comments.author: Alexander Terp

comments.body: Done in 4a17f901: the banner stack is a scroll view bounded to the panes' height (per-window BannerRoom), so it never stands taller than the window; the 8-source-line cap is unchanged and the owner's question about much smaller banners stays open. The cause was SwiftUI centering a stack taller than its frame, not a constraint conflict. Not verified without a real window: trackpad scrolling, the first banner's header in a short window, the 6 pt gutter, and whether the horizontal offset seen on 2026-11-06 is gone.
comments.author: Alexander Terp

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Seen on 0.22.0 (2026-11-06), in a full-screen window with two banners up, each a long message from an agent: a few sentences, a numbered list of five items, a closing paragraph. The stack was drawn near the middle of the panes rather than against their top right, and its top was cut off by the window's top edge, so the first banner began mid-sentence and its header (group, author, Open, dismiss) could not be seen or clicked.

Confirmed from the code: nothing bounds the stack's drawn height. `banners::LINES` caps a banner at 8 Markdown source lines (`markdown::leading`), not drawn lines. Agents write a paragraph or a list item as one long source line, and at the stack's 380-point width each one wraps to 4-8 drawn lines, so two such banners can stand taller than the window. `BannerStackView` has no scroll view or maximum height, and `WindowLayout.attach(banners:)` pins the hosting view's top to the panes' top and its bottom `lessThanOrEqualTo` their bottom, both required, against the hosting view's intrinsic height.

Inferred, not reproduced: once the intrinsic height exceeds the space, those constraints conflict, and either AppKit breaks one (leaving the view placed arbitrarily, which would explain the horizontal position too) or the hosting view is squeezed and SwiftUI centers the overflowing stack, pushing its top out of view. Not checked on a Mac. The horizontal offset is the part least explained.

Repro: post two messages to `@human`, each eight source lines whose lines are ~300 characters, into a window of ordinary height.

Costs: the newest banner's header and the Open button go off screen, so the message can be answered only through its reply field or the conversation, and the stack covers the middle of a pane.

Possibly: cap the stack at the panes' height and scroll inside it, or count the cap in drawn lines (or characters) rather than source lines, and lower the bottom constraint below the hosting view's compression resistance so the stack never fights the panes' frame.
title: The banner stack can stand taller than the window, and is then drawn off its corner with its top cut off
